Subject: HealthLytics hosted pricing — post-demo quantitative next steps

Hi Priya — thanks again for taking the demo this morning. Quick recap of the quantitative items we discussed so we have alignment before I put together a formal hosted pricing sketch: 

- Expected steady-state: ~120M tokens/month (customer estimate in demo).
- Primary traffic profile: long-form summarization + knowledge retrieval (avg token length per request ~1.4k).
- Peak TPS window: occasional spikes up to ~420 TPS (bursts tied to morning ingest + scheduled batch requests), sustained peak target ~280 TPS for 10–15 minute windows.
- Acceptable latency SLO: 250–350ms p95 for generation endpoints (they indicated sub-350ms is required).
- Target unit economics: the internal product team is aiming for $10–$13 per 1M tokens as the acceptable procurement target; finance suggested a budget envelope of $1.0k–$1.8k/mo to start, with room to scale.

Can you confirm the 120M tokens/month and the 420 TPS burst ceiling? Also please attach the traffic breakdown spreadsheet you referenced — that will let us run more precise sizing for hosted slabs and any reserve capacity.

Next steps (proposed):
1) You send the detailed traffic spreadsheet (per-endpoint token distribution + hourly profile).
2) We run a cost/latency sizing and return 2 hosted pricing options: (A) conservative slab with burst allowance, (B) committed monthly with a lower $/1M target.
3) If you prefer, we can include a 30-day canary with volume-based credits to validate latency under your real load.

I’ll loop in Marissa and Karthik to draft the pricing sketch once we get the sheet.

Thanks,
Jonas
--

Jonas — thanks for the write-up and for a crisp demo. Confirming the numbers from our side:
- Monthly: baseline 120M tokens, expected growth to 220M over 6 months if experiments go well.
- Peak: we saw internal tests hit ~430 TPS for 60s in our staging run; customer-facing spikes are probably <=420 TPS as you wrote.
- Latency: p95 target <350ms.
- Budget: initial procurement was $1.2k–$1.6k/mo but finance is flexible if we can justify unit cost and QoS.

Attached: HealthLytics_Monthly_Projection_202610.xlsx — has per-endpoint token counts, hourly distribution, and a 6-month ramp scenario. Also included HL_Redwood_QA_Notes.txt with a short list of compliance questions we expect procurement to ask.

Next: happy to take your hosted sketch. Two asks from procurement: show (1) how burst allowance is charged/limited, and (2) what automatic fallback looks like if Redwood Dedicated is unavailable (they want an SLA-based behavior description).

Thanks — Priya

Subject: Fwd: HealthLytics hosted pricing — post-demo quantitative next steps

Forwarding Priya's confirmation and the projection file. Key asks from procurement: burst charging/limits and fallback behavior. Quick internal proposal below — please comment and I will send to Priya as a formal pricing sketch.

Internal proposal (sketch):
- Option A (Conservative hosted slab): 120M committed tokens/month at $12.50 per 1M tokens. Includes 300 TPS guaranteed throughput with ability to burst to 450 TPS for short windows (burst pool subject to throttling; overage billed at $18/1M tokens prorated). Can include a 14-day ramp buffer (no overage first 14 days for onboarding).
- Option B (Committed growth): 180M committed tokens/month at $11.00 per 1M tokens. Guaranteed 350 TPS sustained with 450 TPS burst pool. Includes 30-day canary credit equal to 10% of committed spend to validate production latency.

Notes: 
- Both options would be hosted API (no VPC). We should prepare a fallback description: routing to a redundant region, automatic model-variant fallback to a lower-cost quantized variant if p95 > 650ms, and on-call escalation workflow. Procurement will want that described concisely.
- Finance asked whether we can provide an introductory 8% discount if they sign a 6-month committed plan.

Marissa / Karthik — any objections to those slab numbers? Is the 450 TPS burst ceiling reasonable given our ripple capacity? Also confirm whether the 8% promotional discount is within your deal approval or if we need leadership sign-off.

Jonas
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: HealthLytics hosted pricing sketch and next steps (attachments)

Hi Priya — attaching the hosted pricing sketch (Redwood_Pricing_Slab_v2.pdf) and a short writeup on fallback/SLA behavior in the same PDF. Summary of the two options we can move forward with: 

Option A (Conservative):
- Commit: 120M tokens/month
- Unit price: $12.50 per 1M tokens (estimated monthly cost $1,500)
- Throughput: 300 TPS guaranteed, burst to 450 TPS short windows
- Onboarding buffer: 14 days of relaxed overage enforcement

Option B (Committed Growth):
- Commit: 180M tokens/month
- Unit price: $11.00 per 1M tokens (estimated monthly cost $1,980)
- Throughput: 350 TPS sustained guarantee, 450 TPS burst pool
- Canary: 30-day canary with credits equal to 10% of committed spend
- Optional: 6-month commit qualifies for an 8% promotional discount (requires legal signature)

We also included the burst billing model and a one-page fallback description (regional routing + model-variant fallback + SLA contact matrix) per your procurement asks.

Proposed next steps:
- You confirm which option (A or B) is closest to your needs and whether procurement wants the 6-month promotional discount included.
- We provide a short mutual action plan and a redlineable term sheet for procurement.
- If you want immediate latency validation, we can schedule a 2-week canary starting as early as Oct 12.

If that all sounds good I’ll get legal and finance to prepare the draft terms.

Best,
Jonas
